chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the impatient false oath leaves the houses deserted.

key_terms.بَلَاقِعُ: Deserted, empty of inhabitants; places devoid of people and livestock — a vivid image of complete desolation and ruin
key_terms.يَمِينُ الصَّبْرِ: The 'oath of endurance' — a technical term in Islamic jurisprudence for an oath sworn before a judge in a legal dispute or under compulsion; also interpreted as a deliberate/willful oath

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about false oaths in legal disputes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns about a specific type of false oath called 'yamin al-sabr' — an oath sworn before a judge or in a legal dispute while enduring pressure. This teaching highlights that perjury in judicial contexts carries devastating social consequences: it causes homes and families to be destroyed and communities to become desolate. The original audience, familiar with pre-Islamic and early Islamic oath-taking customs, would understand this as a grave warning against using legal oaths as instruments of oppression or falsehood.
